t: This is the Whittington Stone, at the foot of Highgate Hill, with a statue of a cat on top. It dates from 1821. The story goes that a forlorn Dick Whittington, heading home from the City after losing heart, heard Bow Bells ringing from four and a half miles away. They seemed to tell him to turn again and become thrice Lord Mayor of London. Two faces of the stone carry that line and a short history of the man. The real Richard Whittington was four times Lord Mayor and paid for drainage in poor areas and a hospital ward for unmarried mothers. The pub next door shares the name.
